## Loading Data

Summary stats and looking at target

Dataset: CPS Annual Social and Economic (March 2026) Supplement for DC

<https://data.census.gov/app/mdat/CPSASEC2026/table?cv=NOW_COV,A_SEX,LJCW,PRWKSTAT&rv=ucgid,A_HGA,PRDISFLG&vv=A_AGE,HUNDER18,FTOTVAL&wt=MARSUPWT&g=AwFm-BVBlBGWg>

Column codes: <https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/cps/techdocs/cpsmar26.pdf>

```{r}
library(readr)
Insurance_data <- read_csv("InsuranceData_correctedcolumns.csv")
```

## Cleaning Data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

df <- Insurance_data |>  select(where(~ !all(is.na(.x))))

# dropping state since all are from DC 
df <- df|> select(-STATE)

# rename columns for clarity, some are kept the same 
df <- df |>
  rename(
    # NOW_COV: 1 = covered, 2 = not covered 
    NOW_COV = NOW_COV, 
    
    # sex: 1 = Male, 2 = Female
    SEX = A_SEX,
    
    # class of longest job 
    # 0 = NIU, 1 = private, 2 = federal, 3 = state, 4 = local, 
    # 5 = self employed incorporated, yes, 6 = self employed incorporated, no or farm
    # 7 = without pay
    LONGEST_JOB_CLASS = LJCW,
    
    # full or part time work 
    # 00 = NIU, 01 = Not in labor force, 02 = FT hours (35+), usually FT
    # 03 = PT for economic reasons, usually FT, 04 = PT for non-economic reasons, usually FT
    # 05 = Not at work, usually FT, 06 = PT hrs, usually PT for economic reasons
    # 07 = PT hrs, usually PT for non-economic, 08 = FT hours, usually PT for economic reasons
    # 09 = FT hours, usually PT for non-economic reasons, 10 = Not at work, usually part-time
    # 11 = Unemployed FT, 12 = Unemployed PT
    FULL_PART_TIME = PRWKSTAT,
    
    # highest grade achieved 
    # 0 = Children, 31 = Less than 1st grade, 32 = 1st,2nd,3rd,or 4th grade
    # 33 = 5th or 6th grade, 34 = 7th and 8th grade, 35 = 9th grade
    # 36 = 10th grade, 37 = 11th grade, 38 = 12th grade no diploma
    # 39 = High school graduate - high school diploma or equivalent
    # 40 = Some college but no degree, 41 = Associate degree in college occupation program
    # 42 = Associate degree in college, 43 = Bachelor's degree, 44 = Master's degree, 
    # 45 = Professional school degree, 46 = Doctorate degree
    EDUCATION = A_HGA, 
    
    # disability 
    # -1 = NIU, 1 = Yes, 2 = No
    DISABILITY = PRDISFLG, 
    
    # age
    AGE = A_AGE,
    
    # Number of persons in household under age 18
    HUNDER18 = HUNDER18, 
    
    # Total family income 
    TOTAL_FAM_INCOME = FTOTVAL
  )

# make response 0 (not covered), 1 (covered)
df$NOW_COV <- ifelse(df$NOW_COV == 1, 1, 0)

summary(df)
```

```{r}

# combining some factor levels 

df <- df |>
  
# education, 1: less than high school, 2: high school, 3: some college, 4: bachelors degree, 5: graduate degree 
  mutate(
    EDUCATION = case_when(
      EDUCATION %in% c(0, 31:38) ~ 1,
      EDUCATION == 39 ~ 2,
      EDUCATION %in% 40:42 ~ 3,
      EDUCATION == 43 ~ 4,
      EDUCATION %in% 44:46 ~ 5,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_),
    
# full or part time, 1: not in labor force, 2: usually full time, 3: usually part time, 4: unemployed 
    FULL_PART_TIME = case_when(
      FULL_PART_TIME %in% c(0, 1) ~ 1,
      FULL_PART_TIME %in% c(2, 5) ~ 2,
      FULL_PART_TIME %in% c(3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10) ~ 3,
      FULL_PART_TIME %in% c(11, 12) ~ 4,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_)) |>

# disability: if NA then -1  
      mutate(DISABILITY = na_if(DISABILITY, -1))

# make columns into factors 
df <- df |> 
  mutate(
    NOW_COV  = factor(NOW_COV),
    SEX    = factor(SEX),
    LONGEST_JOB_CLASS     = factor(LONGEST_JOB_CLASS),
    FULL_PART_TIME = factor(FULL_PART_TIME),
    EDUCATION    = factor(EDUCATION),
    DISABILITY    = factor(DISABILITY)
  )


```

## Splitting Data

```{r}

# split into training and testing 
set.seed(123)

# want to use 80-20 split 
training_pct <- 0.8

# split the data 
Z <- sample(nrow(df), floor(training_pct * nrow(df))) 
df_training <- df[Z, ]
df_testing  <- df[-Z, ]

# view split 
nrow(df_training)
nrow(df_testing)

```

## Logistic Regression Model

#### Log log regression model with step-wise predictor selection

```{r}

# create full loglog regression model (suggestion from Professor Lu)
full_loglog_model <- glm(NOW_COV ~ . , data = df_training, family = binomial(link = "cloglog"))

#run stepwise  
# hide the multiple from step glm.fit: fitted probabilities numerically 0 or 1 occurred warning
suppressWarnings( 
step_loglog_model <- step(full_loglog_model, direction = "both", trace = 0))

# best model from stepwise 
best_loglog_model <- glm(NOW_COV ~ LONGEST_JOB_CLASS + EDUCATION + DISABILITY + AGE + TOTAL_FAM_INCOME, data = df_training, family = binomial(link = "cloglog"))
summary(best_loglog_model)
```

#### ROC curve and cutoff tuning

The cutoff value chosen to combat the accuracy metric problem is 0.97812.

```{r}

# ROC function from 3_KnnLogistic 
roc.analysis <-function (object, newdata = NULL, newplot=TRUE)
{
  if (is.null(newdata)) {
    pi.tp <- object$fitted[object$y == 1]
    pi.tn <- object$fitted[object$y == 0]
  }
  else {
    pi.tp <- predict(object, newdata, type = "response")[newdata$y == 1]
    pi.tn <- predict(object, newdata, type = "response")[newdata$y == 0]
  }
  pi.all <- sort(c(pi.tp, pi.tn))
  sens <- rep(1, length(pi.all)+1)
  specc <- rep(1, length(pi.all)+1)
  for (i in 1:length(pi.all)) {
    sens[i+1] <- mean(pi.tp >= pi.all[i], na.rm = T)
    specc[i+1] <- mean(pi.tn >= pi.all[i], na.rm = T)
  }
  npoints <- length(sens)
  area <- sum(0.5 * (sens[-1] + sens[-npoints]) * (specc[-npoints] -
                                                     specc[-1]))
  lift <- (sens - specc)[-1]
  cutoff <- pi.all[lift == max(lift)][1]
  sensopt <- sens[-1][lift == max(lift)][1]
  specopt <- 1 - specc[-1][lift == max(lift)][1]
  par(pty="s")
  if (newplot){
    plot(specc, sens, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), type = "s",
         xlab = "FPR = 1-specificity", ylab = "TPR = sensitivity", main="ROC")
    abline(0, 1)
  }
  else lines(specc, sens, type="s", lty=2, col=2)
  list(pihat=as.vector(pi.all), sens=as.vector(sens[-1]),
       spec=as.vector(1-specc[-1]), area = area, cutoff = cutoff,
       sensopt = sensopt, specopt = specopt)
}

# view plot 
train.ROC <- roc.analysis(best_loglog_model)

# view results 
train.ROC[(4:7)]

# get cutoff value 
cutoff <- train.ROC$cutoff

```

#### Testing Data Analysis

The testing classification rate is 0.6439169, and the testing error rate is 0.3560831.

```{r}

# get predictions 
loglog_pred_prob <- predict(best_loglog_model, newdata= df_testing, type="response")
loglog_predicted_class <- 1*(loglog_pred_prob > cutoff)

# Confusion matrix
table(df_testing$NOW_COV, loglog_predicted_class)

# Correct classification rate
mean(df_testing$NOW_COV == loglog_predicted_class, na.rm = TRUE)

# Error rate
1 - mean(df_testing$NOW_COV == loglog_predicted_class, na.rm = TRUE)

```

## LDA and QDA Models

### LDA 

```{r}
lda_model <- lda(NOW_COV ~ AGE + HUNDER18 + TOTAL_FAM_INCOME, data = df_training, CV=TRUE)
summary(lda_model)
```

```{r}
mean(lda_model$class != df_training$NOW_COV)
```

### QDA

```{r}
qda_model <- qda(NOW_COV ~ AGE + HUNDER18 + TOTAL_FAM_INCOME, data = df_training, CV=TRUE)
summary(qda_model)
```

```{r}
mean(qda_model$class != df_training$NOW_COV)
```

Both the QDA and LDA models appear to perform the same as the training prediction error rate of 0.033 is the same across both models.
